title: RAW UNREVIEWED: the two f95v plant panels encode a shared subject or two separate entries
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. The already admitted original views Yale 1006242 and 1006243 show visibly different plant drawings under separate text regions; the earlier native orientation explicitly did not establish the f95v1 assignment for 1006242 or a botanical identity. Treat this as a dual-panel discourse architecture, not as another flower/fruit frequency test. First independently settle exact panel identity and, if possible, whether historical botanical iconography intentionally presents one subject in two states or two subjects. Then freeze both full exposed text regions, picture-defined organ contrasts and all-reader whole-form constructions before proposing a reading. A one-subject state account predicts a stable complete subject expression or licensed anaphoric replacement across panels plus a directed state/organ contrast in the passages; two separate entries predict autonomous introductions without a required cross-panel referent and may share only generic article constructions. A contrary reused whole on clearly different objects, or no directional text relation despite a secure one-subject picture, counts against the relevant account. No plant name or Voynich lexeme is inferred now. The missing panel crosswalk, independent same-subject judgment and text-to-image owner are explicit blockers; GDT1083's same-page label/prose failure and IDEA632's single-entry season model are not repaired or selected.

design.prediction: A secure one-referent identification requires both a cross-panel referential link in complete-word/phrase behavior and a directed state/organ relation; two-entry reading requires independent introductions and no such link. Generic template recurrence alone favors neither.
